topic: Studentized sequential rerandomization for joint spillover and carryover inference. In even-G partial-interference groups observed over two-period blocks, randomize half the groups to each of two saturation levels using a predictable soft-rerandomization kernel applied to the exactly standardized complete-randomization imbalance, then assign fixed treatment counts within groups. For bounded nonanticipating lag-one potential outcomes and logged conditional inclusion probabilities, prove exact joint HT unbiasedness for direct and spillover effects, derive a root-GB martingale/combinatorial CLT, construct an observable conservative 2-by-2 studentizer and simultaneous Wald coverage, and prove Omega_RR=Omega_CR-(1-v_eta,kappa)P with the displayed standard-normal tilt constant and P the limiting projection covariance. Use the projection criterion to characterize every strictly improved contrast and retain the Yu--Ma--Liu/Bojinov--Shephard market experiment as a prospective design consumer, not a retrospective growing-G validation.

open_problems.open_problem: Does a history-uniform finite-population Gaussian approximation hold for every bounded balanced-sign three-vector of two causal-score coordinates and one standardized imbalance, strongly enough to transfer soft-tilt-weighted quadratic moments when the score covariance is singular?

source_refs.claim: Gives vector finite-population CLTs for randomization estimators, but not a history-uniform tilted quadratic-moment approximation at singular covariance.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Uses Stein's method for Berry--Esseen bounds on linear and quadratic permutation statistics, without predictable soft-tilt weighting or singular-support moment transport.
source_refs.author: Lei Shi and Peng Ding

source_refs.claim: Obtains stratified linear-permutation Berry--Esseen bounds with heterogeneous strata, but not vector soft-tilt-weighted second moments on a covariance support.
source_refs.author: Pengfei Tian, Fan Yang, and Peng Ding

source_refs.excerpt: State an explicit conditional sampling-without-replacement transport stability lemma

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web literature controls distributional error for finite-population permutation statistics, while the prior reviewer request identifies conditional sampling-without-replacement transport as a missing adaptive-design lemma. Here the approximation metric must be strengthened from scalar Kolmogorov or smooth bounded tests to expectations of an unbounded quadratic score multiplied by a predictable radial tilt, uniformly over histories. Inverse whitening is unavailable when the two-score covariance is singular, so the proof must first project onto the covariance range and obtain uniform integrability there; no located result supplies that combination.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform Berry--Esseen or smooth-test theorem for the balanced-sign three-vector, formulated on the covariance range, with an explicit o(1) bound for the difference between its soft-tilt-weighted score quadratic moments and the corresponding Gaussian moments under a finite-population leverage condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It ties the probability lemma to the concrete joint spillover-and-carryover design payoff rather than presenting a detached normal-approximation problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: joint spillover/carryover estimators need a design CLT -> soft sequential balance reweights balanced assignments -> ordinary weak convergence does not transfer weighted second moments -> a history-uniform singular-support Gaussian approximation is required

method_exemplars.technique: Represent finite-population estimators as linear permutation statistics and use Stein couplings to control linear and quadratic functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An exactly balanced half-sample sign vector is a permutation statistic, and the desired score/imbalance tuple is fixed-dimensional; the new proof must add predictable tilting and covariance-range reduction.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply Cramer--Wold finite-population CLTs under maximum-unit leverage conditions and track the randomization covariance of vector estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the natural triangular-array regularity and vector covariance objects that the weighted-moment approximation must strengthen.

method_exemplars.technique: Use stratum-preserving permutation couplings and concentration to obtain Berry--Esseen bounds with heterogeneous finite populations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditioning on block histories produces heterogeneous finite populations analogous to strata, although the destination requires a vector and tilted moments.

open_problems.open_problem: Can predictable complement-symmetric soft rerandomization of exactly half the groups between two saturation levels preserve exact joint Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness and support root-GB studentized simultaneous inference for direct and spillover effects under bounded lag-one partial interference?

source_refs.claim: Develops a two-stage minimax design, HT asymptotics, and conservative variances for joint spillover and carryover, but not predictable soft sequential rerandomization.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Wei Ma, and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: Introduces sequential rerandomization and proves balance gains, without spillover estimands, temporal carryover, or a joint studentized design-based limit law.
source_refs.author: Quan Zhou, Philip A. Ernst, Kari Lock Morgan, Donald B. Rubin, and Anru Zhang

source_refs.claim: Establishes finite-population IPW/AIPW martingale inference for adaptive designs, including sequential rerandomization, but not two-stage exposure mappings with joint spillover and carryover.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Anqi Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: Add a selected-design variance estimator plus a design-based limit-law and coverage statement
Conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, its triangular-array influence coordinates are phi_{c,k}^{CR}.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest web papers separate the necessary layers: Yu--Ma--Liu treat spillover and carryover under a fixed minimax two-stage design, Zhou et al. treat sequential rerandomization as a balance device, and Li--Zhao treat general adaptive finite-population inference without the dependent exposure categories induced by fixed within-group counts. The prior catalogue independently leaves selected-design covariance and coverage open while supplying only a nonadaptive fixed-count vector CLT. The missing proof must combine a history-dependent balanced-sign score with conditionally centered within-group sampling noise, show their cross covariance vanishes, and obtain an observable PSD-conservative joint covariance despite unobserved cross-potential-outcome terms.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-population theorem giving exact joint HT unbiasedness from logged conditional exposure probabilities, a bivariate root-GB martingale/combinatorial CLT, an observable PSD-conservative 2-by-2 covariance estimator, and asymptotically valid simultaneous Wald coverage.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation directly joins spatial spillovers and temporal carryover in multi-unit experiments and exposes adaptive balance as the missing design layer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: multi-unit interventions violate no-interference -> temporal persistence invalidates static exposure comparisons -> two-stage designs target direct and spillover effects -> predictable soft rerandomization must add precision without losing joint design-based inference

method_exemplars.technique: Use two-stage exposure probabilities to define and unbiasedly estimate direct and indirect finite-population effects under partial interference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired HT vector uses the same saturation-conditioned exposure categories, with the first-stage law replaced by a predictable soft kernel and lagged histories.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct predictable IPW martingale increments, prove conditional-variance stabilization, and estimate a conservative finite-population covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed assignments are adaptive with logged propensities, but the increment must be enlarged to the joint direct/spillover score and decomposed through fixed-count within-group assignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive joint randomization-based HT covariance formulas and conservative variance estimators for two-stage direct and spillover contrasts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its causal vector and missing cross-potential-outcome covariance problem match the requested studentizer, while the destination adds predictable dependence and carryover.

open_problems.open_problem: For predictable radial soft rerandomization of exactly balanced group saturations, is the direct/spillover covariance reduction exactly a scalar shrinkage of the imbalance projection, with strict improvement precisely for contrasts correlated with that imbalance?

source_refs.claim: Shows that hard Mahalanobis rerandomization contracts only the outcome component projected onto covariate imbalance and gives an explicit truncated-Gaussian variance reduction.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Develops projection-based design theory for static cluster rerandomization, but not adaptive saturation assignments, carryover, or a joint direct/spillover vector.
source_refs.author: Xin Lu, Tianle Liu, Hanzhong Liu, and Peng Ding

source_refs.claim: Optimizes two-stage designs for direct and spillover effects under carryover, but does not characterize the covariance effect of a predictable soft imbalance tilt.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Wei Ma, and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.excerpt: Scoped out of v1: graph families beyond two-block, the fixed-treatment-count design class
the realizable randomized +-1 designs are a strict subset

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hard rerandomization has a static truncated-Gaussian projection decomposition, whereas a predictable soft kernel reweights an exactly balanced sign law block by block and the causal score includes additional within-group fixed-count noise. The prior catalogue also warns that fixed-cardinality laws occupy a strict covariance subset and were excluded from its realizability theorem. The first missing step is therefore to prove that the soft tilt changes only the limiting imbalance projection while the within-group covariance and cross term remain unchanged, and to show that this projected covariance is implementable under the fixed-half support before passing the identity through the martingale sum.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A covariance theorem Omega_soft = Omega_complete - (1-v_eta,kappa)P with an explicit standard-normal soft-tilt constant and an implementable PSD projection covariance P, plus the equivalence that a contrast c is strictly improved exactly when c'P c > 0.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative makes rerandomization valuable through transparent projection geometry and an explicit variance-reduction factor.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: complete randomization permits chance imbalance -> rerandomization contracts the imbalance distribution -> only outcome variation aligned with imbalance is reduced -> soft sequential saturation balance needs an equally explicit contrast-level gain criterion

method_exemplars.technique: Orthogonally decompose the joint Gaussian limit of the outcome estimator and imbalance, then compute conditional covariance of the projected component under rerandomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested identity is the soft-tilt, sequential, vector-effect analogue of this projection calculation.

method_exemplars.technique: Aggregate outcomes to cluster totals, derive joint cluster-level limits with imbalance, and quantify covariance contraction under cluster rerandomization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Groups are the first-stage randomization units, so its cluster-total reduction is the nearest static precursor to the balanced-sign block score.

method_exemplars.technique: Use semidefinite geometry and rounding under a global cardinality constraint to characterize implementable balanced-sign moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact half allocation imposes the fixed-cardinality moment geometry that a Gaussian projection calculation alone does not certify.

open_problems.open_problem: When the analysis carryover order is shorter than the true order, can predictable two-saturation rerandomization support sharp finite-population bias bounds and honest simultaneous regions for direct and spillover effects rather than only a CLT centered at a biased pseudo-target?

source_refs.claim: Shows that underspecifying carryover order introduces non-negligible asymptotic bias and makes conservative variance estimation from observed data challenging.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Wei Ma, and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: Studies optimal switchback design and inference under carryover-order misspecification for one aggregate experimental unit, not joint direct/spillover effects in partial-interference groups.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: Defines lagged finite-population dynamic effects and gives unbiased estimators and conservative inference under known assignment-path probabilities, without simultaneous spatial spillovers.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, Ashesh Rambachan, and Neil Shephard

open_problems.why_unsolved: Yu--Ma--Liu isolate the concrete failure: if the specified lag is below the true lag, the HT statistic is centered on an expectation differing from the intended effect and unobserved longer histories obstruct an observable conservative variance. Switchback and panel-experiment results provide dynamic estimands and misspecification analyses but do not combine randomized saturation, within-group spillovers, and predictable rerandomization. Bounded potential outcomes create a route to partial information, but the omitted-history configurations must be optimized jointly with the known adaptive assignment law rather than treated as an unrestricted additive bias.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified set or computable finite-population upper and lower bias bounds for each direct/spillover coordinate under an explicit longer-lag sensitivity class, together with a uniformly valid joint confidence region combining those bounds with design-based sampling uncertainty.

writing_exemplar.why: It states the underspecified-lag bias problem inside the destination model and makes the loss of feasible variance estimation explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: carryover order determines valid exposure histories -> over-specification costs precision but preserves the target -> under-specification changes the estimator's expectation -> bounded-history information should yield honest bias-aware joint inference

method_exemplars.technique: Index finite-population causal contrasts by treatment histories and express unbiased estimators through known path probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Longer treatment histories make the omitted carryover contribution to the target-minus-pseudo-target discrepancy explicit.

method_exemplars.technique: Separate design variance from carryover-order misspecification in finite-population switchback risk and construct conservative randomization-based inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proof architecture must be generalized from one time series to multiple saturation-randomized groups and a two-coordinate spillover estimand.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose HT expectation and variance under correct, over-specified, and under-specified carryover orders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its under-specification decomposition is the natural starting constraint system for sharp bias bounds under the proposed adaptive design.

open_problems.open_problem: Can Gaussian prepivoting yield a test that is finite-sample exact for joint sharp nulls and asymptotically conservative for joint weak nulls on direct and spillover effects under predictable soft sequential rerandomization with lag-one carryover?

source_refs.claim: Shows that studentization can fail under rerandomization and develops Gaussian prepivoting that is exact under sharp nulls and asymptotically valid under weak nulls in standard rerandomized designs.
source_refs.author: Peter L. Cohen and Colin B. Fogarty
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B

source_refs.claim: Builds studentized randomization tests exact under compatible sharp nulls and conservative under weak nulls for factorial, stratified, and clustered experiments.
source_refs.author: Jason Wu and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Provides joint Wald procedures for direct and spillover effects in static two-stage experiments, but not exact-to-weak-null tests under adaptive rerandomization and carryover.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Kosuke Imai, and Anup Malani

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cohen--Fogarty show that under restricted randomization a studentized statistic alone need not align the weak-null sampling law with the sharp-null randomization law. The destination design adds history-dependent acceptance weights, exactly balanced group totals, fixed-count within-group exposure randomization, and a bivariate causal null. The first altered proof step is the Gaussian reference measure: it must be conditioned on the predictable soft kernel and paired with a conservative 2-by-2 completion while stochastic domination is proved uniformly over histories and remains meaningful at singular limiting covariance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit bivariate Gaussian-prepivoted randomization statistic whose conditional p-value is exact under a joint sharp null and whose rejection probability is asymptotically at most alpha under the corresponding joint weak null, including singular limiting covariance.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the conflict between sharp-null exactness and weak-null validity and explains why plain studentization can be inadequate under rerandomization.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: randomization tests are exact for imputable sharp nulls -> scientific targets are weak average-effect nulls -> restricted randomization can defeat ordinary studentization -> Gaussian prepivoting must be rebuilt for adaptive joint spillover/carryover inference

method_exemplars.technique: Map a statistic through a conservative Gaussian probability computed jointly with the balance statistic, then prove sharp-null exactness and weak-null stochastic domination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same calibration can incorporate a soft acceptance weight and the conservative direct/spillover covariance completion.

method_exemplars.technique: Impute under a compatible sharp null, studentize a multivariate contrast, and compare its randomization and sampling limits under finite-population heterogeneity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its multiple-outcome and clustered extensions are the nearest template for a joint causal vector, though not for interference plus adaptive rerandomization.

method_exemplars.technique: Form joint tests of direct and spillover contrasts using conservative design-based covariance matrices.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the destination contrast geometry and covariance ordering to place inside the prepivot.

literature_map:
Hudgens--Halloran (2008, JASA) is the foundational two-stage partial-interference source for direct, indirect, total, and overall effects.
Basse--Feller (2018, JASA) derives unbiased individual- and household-weighted estimators and randomization variances for practical two-stage experiments.
Jiang--Imai--Malani (2023, Biometrics) supplies joint direct/spillover inference and conservative covariance estimation under static two-stage randomization.
Jizhou Liu (2026, Journal of Econometrics) adds two-stage covariate-adaptive randomization, but through static fine stratification without carryover.
Yu--Ma--Liu (2025, arXiv:2501.14602) is the closest destination paper: minimax two-stage design, HT inference, spillover plus carryover, and an underspecified-lag bias problem.
Bojinov--Shephard (2019, JASA) defines time-series causal estimands and exact randomization tests, motivated by randomized market experiments.
Bojinov--Rambachan--Shephard (2021, Quantitative Economics) extends dynamic effects, unbiased estimation, and finite-population inference to panels.
Bojinov--Simchi-Levi--Zhao (2023, Management Science) gives minimax switchback design and carryover-robust inference, but not joint spatial spillovers.
Morgan--Rubin (2012, Annals of Statistics) and Li--Ding--Rubin (2018, PNAS) establish rerandomization and its projection/truncated-Gaussian precision geometry.
Zhou--Ernst--Morgan--Rubin--Zhang (2018, Biometrika) develops sequential rerandomization for batch enrollment, focusing on balance rather than interference.
Lu--Liu--Liu--Ding (2023, Biometrika) extends design-based rerandomization theory to clusters and regression adjustment, without saturation spillovers.
Li--Zhao (2026, arXiv:2602.21998) supplies finite-population IPW/AIPW martingale theory for adaptive designs, including sequential rerandomization, but not lagged two-stage interference.
Wu--Ding (2021, JASA) and Cohen--Fogarty (2022, JRSSB) connect sharp-null exactness to weak-null validity and show why rerandomization needs more than naive studentization.
Li--Ding (2017, JASA), Shi--Ding (2026, Annals of Statistics), and Tian--Yang--Ding (2025, arXiv:2503.13986) give finite-population Gaussian approximations, but not history-uniform soft-tilt-weighted quadratic moments at singular covariance.
No located paper jointly covers predictable soft rerandomization, fixed within-group saturation counts, lag-one carryover, a bivariate direct/spillover HT score, a conservative 2-by-2 studentizer, and the exact projection covariance identity.
